concepts.name: Angle sum of a quadrilateral
concepts.description: The four interior angles of any quadrilateral always add up to 360°.

concepts.name: Classifying quadrilaterals
concepts.description: Quadrilaterals are classified by their side and angle properties: parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares and trapeziums each have distinctive properties.

concepts.name: Parallelograms
concepts.description: Opposite sides are equal and parallel, opposite angles are equal, and consecutive angles are supplementary.

concepts.name: Rectangles and squares
concepts.description: A rectangle has four right angles and equal diagonals; a square is a rectangle with all four sides equal.

concepts.name: Rhombuses
concepts.description: A rhombus has four equal sides, and its diagonals bisect each other at right angles.

formulas.title: Angle sum of a quadrilateral
formulas.prompt: What do the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to?
formulas.explanation: This holds for every quadrilateral, no matter its shape.
formulas.example: If three angles are 80°, 95° and 100°, the fourth is 360 − 80 − 95 − 100 = 85°
formulas.commonMistake: Confusing the quadrilateral angle sum (360°) with the triangle angle sum (180°).
formulas.applicationPrompt: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 100°. Find the fourth.

formulas.title: Parallelogram angles
formulas.prompt: How are the angles of a parallelogram related?
formulas.formula: Opposite angles are equal; consecutive angles sum to 180°
formulas.explanation: Opposite sides being parallel means each pair of consecutive angles forms a co-interior pair, which is why they are supplementary.
formulas.example: If one angle is 65°, the adjacent angle is 180 − 65 = 115°, and the opposite angle is also 65°.
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming all four angles are equal, as in a rectangle.
formulas.applicationPrompt: One angle of a parallelogram is 65°. Find the angle next to it.

formulas.title: Rectangle diagonals
formulas.prompt: How do the diagonals of a rectangle compare?
formulas.formula: Diagonals are equal in length: AC = BD
formulas.explanation: Unlike a general parallelogram, a rectangle's diagonals are always equal (though they still bisect each other).
formulas.example: If diagonal AC = 10 cm, diagonal BD is also 10 cm.
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming the diagonals are also perpendicular, which is only true for a square.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A rectangle has diagonal AC = 10 cm. Find diagonal BD.

formulas.title: Rhombus side from diagonals
formulas.prompt: How can you find the side of a rhombus from its diagonals?
formulas.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by the two half-diagonals.
formulas.example: Half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm: side = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm
formulas.commonMistake: Using the full diagonals instead of half-diagonals in the formula.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A rhombus has diagonals meeting at right angles with half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm. Find the side length.

formulas.title: Rhombus from its diagonals
formulas.prompt: You know a rhombus's diagonals. What are its side and area?
formulas.formula:
Side = ½√(d₁² + d₂²)
Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂
formulas.explanation: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making four right triangles.
formulas.example: Diagonals 16 and 12: halves 8 and 6, side 10, area 96.
formulas.commonMistake: Using the full diagonals as the legs of the right triangle.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A rhombus has side 13 and one diagonal 24. Find its area.

formulas.title: Rectangle diagonals by triplets
formulas.prompt: What is the quick way to a rectangle's diagonal?
formulas.explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the two sides as legs.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A rectangle's diagonal is 17 and one side is 8. Find its area.

levels.title: Every Quadrilateral Sums to 360°
levels.description: The four interior angles of any quadrilateral always add up to 360°.

blocks.title: A fact true for every quadrilateral
blocks.body: No matter how a four-sided shape is stretched, its interior angles always sum to exactly 360° — twice the triangle angle sum, since any quadrilateral can be split into two triangles.

blocks.title: Angle sum
blocks.caption: This holds for every quadrilateral: square, rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium or any irregular four-sided shape.

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 80°, angle B = 95°, angle C = 100°. What is angle D?
questions.context: Study the quadrilateral and answer the question.

figure.caption: Quadrilateral ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Quadrilateral ABCD with angles marked A: 80°, B: 95°, C: 100°, D: ?.

questions.explanation: The four angles sum to 360°: angle D = 360 − 80 − 95 − 100 = 85°.
questions.method: Subtract the three known angles from 360°.

hints.text: The four angles of any quadrilateral always sum to 360°.

commonMistakes: Using 180° instead of 360° as the total.

questions.question: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal, and opposite angles equal, is called a

figure.caption: Parallelogram ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Parallelogram ABCD, with AB marked parallel to DC and AD marked equal in length to BC.

questions.explanation: A parallelogram is defined by having both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal, which also makes opposite angles equal.
solutionSteps: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal → parallelogram.
questions.method: Match the description to the defining shape.

hints.text: A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

commonMistakes: Confusing a parallelogram with a trapezium, which has only one pair of parallel sides.

questions.question: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD are always equal in length. If AC = 10 cm, what is BD?

figure.caption: Rectangle ABCD with diagonals
figure.ariaSummary: Rectangle ABCD with both diagonals AC and BD drawn, and right angles marked at all four corners.

questions.explanation: A rectangle's two diagonals are always equal, so BD = AC = 10 cm.
solutionSteps: Diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
questions.method: Use the equal-diagonals property of a rectangle.

hints.text: This property is unique to rectangles (and squares) among parallelograms.

commonMistakes: Trying to compute BD from side lengths that were never given.

questions.question: In parallelogram ABCD, consecutive angles A and B are supplementary. If angle A = 65°, what is angle B?
questions.context: Study the parallelogram and answer the question.

figure.caption: Parallelogram ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Parallelogram ABCD with angle A marked 65° and angle B marked ?; AB is parallel to DC, and AD equals BC.

questions.explanation: Consecutive angles in a parallelogram sum to 180°: angle B = 180 − 65 = 115°.

hints.text: AD and BC are parallel, and AB crosses them: angles A and B are co-interior, so they add up to 180°.

commonMistakes: Assuming angle B equals angle A, as if it were the opposite angle.

questions.question: In rhombus ABCD, the diagonals bisect each other at right angles at O. If OA = 3 cm and OB = 4 cm, find the length of side AB.

figure.caption: Rhombus ABCD with diagonals
figure.ariaSummary: Rhombus ABCD with all four sides tick-marked equal, and diagonals AC and BD crossing at right angles at O.

questions.explanation: Triangle OAB is right-angled at O, so AB = √(OA² + OB²) = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
questions.method: Apply the Pythagorean relationship to the right triangle formed by the two half-diagonals.

hints.text: OA, OB and AB form a right triangle since the diagonals meet at 90°.

commonMistakes: Adding OA and OB directly instead of using the Pythagorean relationship.

questions.question: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to DC, and AD is a leg joining them. Angle A and angle D lie on the same leg, so they are supplementary. If angle A = 70°, what is angle D?
questions.context: Study the trapezium and answer the question.

figure.caption: Trapezium ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Trapezium ABCD with AB parallel to DC; angle A marked 70° and angle D marked with a question mark.

questions.explanation: Angles on the same leg between a pair of parallel sides are supplementary: angle D = 180 − 70 = 110°.

hints.text: AB and DC are parallel, and AD is the transversal joining them.

commonMistakes: Assuming angle D equals angle A.

questions.question: Which quadrilateral has all four sides equal in length, but its angles are not necessarily 90°?
questions.explanation: A rhombus has all four sides equal, but its angles can be anything (a square is the special case where they are all 90°).
solutionSteps: All sides equal, angles not necessarily 90° → rhombus.
questions.method: Match the side/angle description to the shape.

hints.text: A square is a rhombus with right angles — but the question says angles are not necessarily 90°.

commonMistakes: Choosing square, which additionally requires right angles.

questions.question: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = (2x + 20)° and angle C = (3x − 10)° are opposite angles, so they are equal. Find angle A.
questions.context: Study the parallelogram and answer the question.

figure.caption: Parallelogram ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Parallelogram ABCD with opposite angle A marked (2x + 20)° and opposite angle C marked (3x − 10)°.

questions.explanation: Opposite angles are equal: 2x + 20 = 3x − 10, so x = 30. Angle A = 2(30) + 20 = 80°.
questions.method: Set the two opposite angles equal, solve for x, then substitute back.

hints.text: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are always equal.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to substitute x back in to find the actual angle.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. Find the length of each side.

figure.caption: Rhombus ABCD with diagonals
figure.ariaSummary: Rhombus ABCD with all four sides tick-marked equal, and diagonals AC and BD crossing at right angles at O.

questions.explanation: Half-diagonals are 8 cm and 6 cm. Side = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 cm.
questions.method: Halve both diagonals first, then apply the Pythagorean relationship.

hints.text: The diagonals bisect each other, so use half of each.

commonMistakes: Using the full diagonals instead of half-diagonals in the Pythagorean step.

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = x°, angle B = 2x°, angle C = 3x° and angle D = 4x°. Find the largest angle.
questions.context: Study the quadrilateral and answer the question.

figure.caption: Quadrilateral ABCD
figure.ariaSummary: Quadrilateral ABCD with angles marked A: x°, B: 2x°, C: 3x°, D: 4x°.

questions.explanation: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°: x + 2x + 3x + 4x = 10x = 360, so x = 36. The largest angle is 4x = 4 × 36 = 144°.
questions.method: Add the four expressions, set the total to 360°, then find 4x.

hints.text: Add the four expressions and set the total equal to 360°.

commonMistakes: Stopping at x = 36 instead of finding the largest angle, 4x.

questions.question: Rectangle ABCD has length AB = 24 cm and breadth BC = 7 cm. Find the length of its diagonal AC.
questions.context: Study the rectangle and answer the question.

figure.caption: Rectangle ABCD, 24 cm by 7 cm, with diagonal AC
figure.ariaSummary: Rectangle ABCD with AB = 24 cm and BC = 7 cm, a right angle marked at B, and diagonal AC drawn dashed and marked ?.

questions.explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of right triangle ABC: AC = √(24² + 7²) = √(576 + 49) = √625 = 25 cm.
questions.method: Use Pythagoras in the right triangle formed by two sides and the diagonal.

hints.text: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 24 cm and 7 cm.

commonMistakes: Adding the sides (24 + 7 = 31) instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.question: Which property is true of every rhombus, but NOT true of every parallelogram?

options.text: Its diagonals are equal in length.
Its diagonals cross at right angles.

questions.explanation: Every parallelogram already has diagonals that bisect each other and equal opposite angles, so those do not single out a rhombus. Equal diagonals belong to rectangles, and a rhombus that is not a square does not have them. Diagonals that cross at right angles hold for every rhombus but fail for a general parallelogram.
solutionSteps: Diagonals bisect each other: true of every parallelogram.
Opposite angles equal: true of every parallelogram.
Equal diagonals: a rectangle property, false for most rhombuses.
Diagonals at right angles: true of every rhombus, not of every parallelogram.
questions.method: Test each property on a slanted parallelogram first, then on a rhombus.

hints.text: Picture a long, slanted parallelogram that is not a rhombus, and see which properties still hold.

commonMistakes: Choosing "diagonals bisect each other", which every parallelogram has.
Confusing the rhombus with the rectangle, whose diagonals are equal.

questions.question: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD meet at O. If angle BOC = 70°, find angle OAB.
questions.context: Study the rectangle and answer the question.

figure.caption: Rectangle ABCD with diagonals meeting at O
figure.ariaSummary: Rectangle ABCD with diagonals AC and BD meeting at O and right angles at all four corners. Angle BOC is marked 70° and angle OAB is marked ?.

questions.explanation: Angle AOB = 180° − 70° = 110°, since AOB and BOC lie on the straight line BD. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so OA = OB and triangle AOB is isosceles. Angle OAB = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°.
solutionSteps: OA = OB, because equal diagonals bisect each other.
questions.method: Use the straight angle at O, then the isosceles triangle AOB.

hints.text: Angles AOB and BOC lie on the straight line BD.
Half of each diagonal is the same length, so OA = OB.

commonMistakes: Answering 55°, which is angle OBC in triangle BOC, not angle OAB.
